english.title: Advertise credit where goods etc are not available for cash
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), indicated, by means of an advertisement to which Part IV of the Consumer Credit Act 1974 applied, a willingness to provide credit under a restricted-use credit agreement relating to

(A)_[goods]_
(B)_[services]_

to be supplied by **(..SPECIFY NAME..), namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS OR SERVICES..), when, at the time the advertisement was published, that supplier was not holding himself out as being prepared to

(C)_[sell those goods]_
(D)_[provide those services]_

for cash
english.legislation: Contrary to section 45 of, and Schedule 1 to, the Consumer Credit Act 1974.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment a fine or both

Time Limit on Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
